advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decode /proc/mounts octal escapes (e.g. \040) before comparing mount points in is_mounted/describe_source, or document that the /proc/mounts fallback does not support whitespace mount points.
evidence: infra/scripts/check-mounts.sh:52: `awk -v mp="$1" '$2 == mp { found = 1 } END { exit found ? 0 : 1 }' /proc/mounts`

Header comment lines 28-31 claim whitespace safety: 'A mount point is a PATH: it may contain whitespace ... splitting one into two bogus targets would make this check report on directories that do not exist'

ABSENCE: search for '040' in the test module returns (no matches); the whitespace test (test_a_mount_point_containing_whitespace_is_one_target_not_two) stubs mountpoint(1), so the /proc/mounts fallback's whitespace behavior is never exercised — /proc/mounts writes such a path as e.g. `/var/my\040volume` which `$2 == "/var/my volume"` will not match
advisory.finding: The /proc/mounts fallback in is_mounted (and describe_source) compares the mount point literally with awk `$2 == mp`, but /proc/mounts encodes whitespace in mount points as the octal escape \040. A mount point containing a space therefore never matches on a host without util-linux, so is_mounted's fallback would report a genuinely-mounted whitespace path as NOT mounted (exit 1) and check-mounts.sh would print the misleading 'plain directory on the ROOT filesystem' FAIL — contradicting the header comment that explicitly promises whitespace-safe handling.
scenarios: Host without util-linux (mountpoint(1) absent) whose EBS volume is mounted at a path containing a space, checked mid-incident
advisory.suggested_fix: In the awk fallbacks, gsub the octal escapes in $2 before comparison, e.g. `{ p=$2; gsub(/\\040/," ",p); gsub(/\\011/,"\t",p) } p == mp`, so the fallback matches the whitespace handling the mountpoint(1) path and the header comment promise.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update infra/terraform/variables.tf's `gate_scratch_mount` description to include infra/scripts/check-mounts.sh's default target list as a consumer that must agree on the mount path (and correct the 'four things' count).
evidence: infra/scripts/check-mounts.sh:37 `set -- /var/gerrit /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch` introduces a new hardcoded consumer of the gate-scratch mount path

infra/terraform/variables.tf:66-69 description: 'Single-sourced here because four things must agree on it — user_data.sh's fstab entry, the review-bot's REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR/TMPDIR, observability.sh's df probe, and the CloudWatch alarm's `mount` dimension. A disagreement between any two of them is a silent fallback to the root filesystem.'
tests/unit/test_user_data_device_resolution_d614.py:681-682 states 'var.gate_scratch_mount's own documentation says four things must agree on that path; this check is a fifth consumer'
advisory.finding: infra/terraform/variables.tf's `gate_scratch_mount` description enumerates the consumers that must agree on the mount path and states 'four things must agree on it', but this change adds check-mounts.sh as a fifth hardcoded consumer of `/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch`, leaving the count and enumeration stale in the surface that documents the contract.
scenarios: An operator or contributor reading variables.tf to enumerate every place the mount path is defined would miss check-mounts.sh's hardcoded default and could change one without the other.
advisory.suggested_fix: In infra/terraform/variables.tf lines 66-69, add infra/scripts/check-mounts.sh's default mount-point list to the enumerated consumers and adjust the count so the description matches the set of consumers the test pins.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the source-grep in test_the_running_host_check_names_both_volumes_by_default with an execution of check-mounts.sh with NO arguments and assert both /var/gerrit and /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch appear in the output.
evidence: check-mounts.sh:36-38 `if [ "$#" -eq 0 ]; then set -- /var/gerrit /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch; fi` — this default-application code is added by the diff and is never executed by any test (all script-level tests pass an explicit path argument).
advisory.finding: test_the_running_host_check_names_both_volumes_by_default asserts by grepping the literal source text of check-mounts.sh ('/var/gerrit' and '/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch' in src) rather than executing the script with no arguments and observing that both defaults are actually checked. The newly-added default-list behavior (`set -- /var/gerrit /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch`) is thus never executed; a behaviour-preserving refactor (deriving the defaults from a variable, reformatting the literal) breaks the test while the behaviour is intact, and a regression that dropped one default from the runtime loop while leaving the string elsewhere in the file would pass.
scenarios: A refactor that derives the default mount points from a shared constant renames/reflows the literal and reddens the test with no behaviour change.
A regression that removes one mount point from the runtime default list but leaves the string in a comment/usage line stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Run `subprocess.run(["bash", str(CHECK_MOUNTS)], ...)` with a fake bin where mountpoint reports both paths mounted, and assert both mount-point strings appear in stdout (and neither is silently dropped).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an end-to-end check-mounts.sh test that removes both mountpoint(1) and /proc/mounts and asserts the 'cannot determine mount state' FAIL message on stderr plus a non-zero exit.
evidence: check-mounts.sh:93-96 `state=$?` then `if [ "$state" -eq 2 ]; then printf 'FAIL  %s: cannot determine mount state ...' "$mount_point" >&2` — added by the diff.

tests/unit/test_user_data_device_resolution_d614.py:874 `script = _check_mounts_functions(absent) + "\nis_mounted /var/gerrit\n"` — invokes the extracted function only, not the script's caller/FAIL branch.

ABSENCE: no test invokes `bash check-mounts.sh <mp>` on a host with neither mountpoint(1) nor a readable /proc/mounts and asserts the 'cannot determine mount state' message on stderr and a non-zero exit.
advisory.finding: The newly-added script-level 'cannot determine mount state' outcome (check-mounts.sh lines 93-96: `state=$?; if [ "$state" -eq 2 ]; then printf 'FAIL ... cannot determine mount state ...'`) is not exercised end-to-end. The only exit-2 test (test_is_mounted_says_it_cannot_tell_rather_than_claiming_not_mounted) calls the extracted is_mounted() function directly and asserts its return code is 2; no test runs the whole script through the caller branch that captures `state=$?`, emits the distinct 'cannot determine mount state' message, and sets failed=1 / exits non-zero.
scenarios: A host without util-linux and without a readable /proc/mounts (the exact incident host the third outcome exists for): the caller-side handling of exit 2 could silently mis-branch (e.g. fall into the `-d` plain-directory message or fail to set failed=1) and no test would catch it.
